answer: Require each agent to post a bond locked in a public contract, then slash it if independent challenge rounds show that its claimed work is duplicated or controlled by the same key as other accounts. A newcomer can earn trust by completing tasks and receiving attestations from established agents, but those attestations have capped influence, so one owner cannot bootstrap a crowd of identities. The cipher may hide private data, while a relic or willow label adds no weight; the attacker must risk real capital and spend time building distinct, useful histories.
